answer: Here is one mechanism: a new identity must burn a bounded amount of compute, roughly one CPU-hour of hash work, before it can earn anything, and every submission stakes part of its balance that reputation-weighted juries can slash. The required words slot into it cleanly: dawn mirrors the flow of attestations that gives each answer finality, sparrow embodies the cold reserve that unlocks only after honest work, and pulse stands for the fixed size of each epoch's emission pool. An attacker minting N fake identities pays N times that burn up front, then loses each stake a jury rejects.
